35 Two batteries are connected together, as shown.
battery 1
battery 2
12 V

0.3 Ω
0.1 Ω
Battery 1 has electromotive force (e.m.f.) 12 V and internal resistance 0.3 Ω.
Battery 2 has e.m.f. 9 V and internal resistance 0.1 Ω.
What are the e.m.f. and the internal resistance of a single battery that has the same effect as the
combination?
e.m.f. / V
internal
resistance / Ω
A
3
0.2
B
3
0.4
C
21
0.2
D
21
0.4

hints: Look at the cell symbols for battery 1 and battery 2 in the diagram - the positive terminals face opposite directions along the series line, so the 12 V and 9 V drives oppose each other.
Recall the series rules: total e.m.f. is the algebraic sum with sign for direction, $E_{total} = E_1 - E_2$ for opposition, while internal resistances always add, $r_{total} = r_1 + r_2$.
Work out $12\text{ V} - 9\text{ V}$ for the net drive and $0.3\ \Omega + 0.1\ \Omega$ for the total lost volts per ampere, then match both values to the same row of the table.
walkthrough: Identify the connection from the diagram. The two dashed battery symbols are in series but reversed relative to each other, so current driven one way round by the $12\text{ V}$ battery is driven the opposite way by the $9\text{ V}$ battery.
State the e.m.f. rule for series cells in opposition. Net e.m.f. is the difference: $E = E_1 - E_2$.
Substitute the values with units: $E = 12\text{ V} - 9\text{ V} = 3\text{ V}$, with the larger $12\text{ V}$ battery determining the overall polarity.
State the internal resistance rule. Resistances in series always add because the same current passes through both: $r = r_1 + r_2$.
Substitute the values: $r = 0.3\ \Omega + 0.1\ \Omega = 0.4\ \Omega$. The terminal p.d. of the equivalent battery is then $V = E - Ir = 3\text{ V} - I(0.4\ \Omega)$, same as for the combination.
A single battery with $3\text{ V}$ e.m.f. and $0.4\ \Omega$ internal resistance matches the combination. This is option B.

A.explanation: The $3\text{ V}$ correctly subtracts the opposing e.m.f.s, but $0.2\ \Omega$ wrongly subtracts the internal resistances which must add in series.

B.explanation: Opposing e.m.f.s give $12\text{ V} - 9\text{ V} = 3\text{ V}$ and series resistances give $0.3\ \Omega + 0.1\ \Omega = 0.4\ \Omega$.

C.explanation: The $21\text{ V}$ adds the e.m.f.s as if the cells aided each other, but the diagram shows the $12\text{ V}$ and $9\text{ V}$ cells connected positive to negative in opposition.

D.explanation: The $0.4\ \Omega$ correctly adds the resistances, but $21\text{ V}$ wrongly adds opposing e.m.f.s instead of subtracting the $9\text{ V}$ from the $12\text{ V}$.
